semantics: V1 configures expiry and refresh, removes expired documents asynchronously, and exposes read-before/read-after expiry and session refresh behavior.
Metadata, cleanup batches, large transactions, sharding, cluster transactions, tombstones, revisions, and replication ordering are observable.
Invalid expiry/refresh values fail without changing the document or lifecycle configuration; refresh never resurrects a deleted document.
public_contract.compatibility: V2 lifecycle timing has explicit limits and remains unresolved until expiry, refresh, and recovery tests exist.

risk.description: Expiry races can expose deleted data or delete a document a concurrent refresh should retain.

semantics: V1 configures archival age/behavior and marks eligible documents while preserving archived metadata through updates and reprocessing.
Batch limits, compression, archive-at parsing, current versus archived state, and malformed configuration errors are observable.
Archival does not change identity, tenant ownership, revisions, attachments, counters, time series, conflicts, or tombstones without an explicit contract.
public_contract.compatibility: V2 archival storage and migration remain unresolved; logical migration preserves archive markers and referenced family data.

risk.description: Archiving a document without family data or metadata makes recovery and queries disagree.

semantics: V1 defines archival interactions with indexes, patches, replication, sharding, smuggler export/import, subscriptions, revisions, and family metadata.
Archived filters and index visibility remain stable while documents update, replicate, restore, or reshard.
Subscription and replication cursors do not skip archival state changes or deliver stale family payloads.
public_contract.compatibility: Each interaction needs an independent V2 contract test; no archival interaction is excluded by default.

risk.description: Archival is cross-family state; inconsistent consumers can expose or omit records after migration.

semantics: V1 configures collection-scoped JSON schema validation, validates existing data on demand, and rejects invalid writes with SchemaValidationException details.
Supported rules include type, required, properties, additional properties, arrays, numbers, strings, constants, enums, references, conditionals, and pattern properties.
Invalid schema definitions, malformed requests, and validation failures are distinct and do not commit rejected documents.
public_contract.compatibility: V2 schema language and error detail must be compared with V1; no silent downgrade to permissive writes is allowed.

risk.description: Validation drift can admit data V1 rejects or reject existing data during migration.

semantics: V1 applies validators during writes and indexing, caches validators by collection, and routes configuration/validation through sharded handlers.
Index/query visibility for invalid or newly configured documents remains consistent across shards and restarts.
Cache invalidation, configuration races, and member loss do not leave one shard using stale rules silently.
public_contract.compatibility: V2 may use a different validator, but observable validation, index, and sharding behavior requires parity tests.

risk.description: Stale validator caches create cross-shard acceptance differences that are hard to repair.

semantics: V1 represents document, attachment, counter, time-series, revision, conflict, and compare-exchange deletion/conflict states with family-specific types and cleanup indexes.
Tombstones carry identity, etags, deletion etags, change vectors, collection, flags, and last-modified state needed for replication and cleanup.
Cleanup waits for configured consumers and does not resurrect stale values or remove unresolved conflicts.
public_contract.compatibility: V2 tombstone schema and retention require recovery and replication receipts; family types cannot be silently collapsed.

risk.description: Tombstone loss is delayed data loss that appears when a stale member rejoins.

semantics: V1 composes documents with attachments, counters, time series, revisions, expiry/refresh, and validation inside session and batch transaction boundaries.
Commit, abort, conflict, retry, and malformed-operation behavior is atomic across affected families.
Replication and recovery expose one coherent transaction marker rather than partial family acknowledgements.
public_contract.compatibility: V2 behavior is tested through the transaction seam while family batch rules remain independently testable.

risk.description: Cross-family partial commits create states V1 clients cannot interpret or repair.

v1_evidence.scope: V1 family query/index paths inspect counters, raw and incremental time series, rollups, tags, values, includes, loaded documents, and projections. Counter and time-series map workers populate index entries, Corax converters serialize family fields, and query retrievers expose family values to the query layer. semantics: V1 query/index paths inspect counters, raw/incremental time series, rollups, tags, values, includes, loaded documents, and projections.
Index maintenance, stale/rebuild behavior, ordering, null/missing state, and multi-family projections are observable.
Indexes do not expose another tenant's family data or bypass schema validation and authorization.
public_contract.compatibility: V2 may use different index structures, but parity tests compare observable results, ordering, errors, and isolation.

risk.description: A family-aware index can return valid-looking but cross-tenant or stale values if ownership is wrong.

semantics: V1 changes/subscriptions deliver mutations for counters, time series, revisions, attachments, archival, conflicts, and deletes.
Batch size, ordering, include ranges, filtering, retries, acknowledgement, failover, cancellation, and malformed payloads are explicit.
A cursor advances only after the required family payload is acknowledged.
public_contract.compatibility: V2 typed streaming preserves family kind, document identity, cursor/change-vector semantics, and authorization.

risk.description: Cursor advancement or retry mistakes permanently skip family changes.

semantics: V1 family handlers reject unauthorized reads, writes, deletes, streams, configuration changes, and acknowledgements with typed security failures.
Tenant/database identity is checked for every family operation, including includes, backup/import, replication administration, sharding, and debug paths.
Failures are auditable and do not reveal family values, attachment bytes, backup contents, or credentials.
public_contract.compatibility: V2 access is through the approved typed Platform Adapter; the engine exposes no private control-plane route or generic HTTP escape hatch.

risk.description: Family data includes large bytes and history, so an authorization bypass has high blast radius.

semantics: V1 family reads support large attachment streams, time-series range paging, typed/asynchronous streaming, bounded reads, and cancellation/disposal.
Size limits, range bounds, position, backpressure, partial consumption, and end-of-stream behavior are independently testable.
Unsupported or over-limit requests return explicit errors and memory remains bounded.
public_contract.compatibility: V2 streaming limits and range syntax require V1 comparison; local timing is not a speed claim.

risk.description: Large payloads expose memory, cancellation, and truncation bugs missed by CRUD tests.

semantics: V1 replication carries family-specific payloads, change vectors, transaction markers, segments, attachment streams, deleted ranges, and tombstones, while sharding routes each family by document identity.
Duplicate, delayed, reordered, dropped, conflicted, member-loss, rejoin, resharding, and cross-shard scenarios define acknowledgement and convergence observations.
Family identity and tenant isolation hold across Regions and Members; unsupported topologies return explicit errors.
public_contract.compatibility: V2 replication algorithm, topology, consistency, and Acknowledgement Levels remain unresolved until parent decision and receipts.

risk.description: Family merge and routing rules are distinct; treating all payloads as generic documents can lose data.

semantics: V1 smuggler/backup paths transfer family payloads, tombstones, conflicts, revisions, expiry/archival metadata, validation configuration, and references.
Full/incremental export, import, restore, interrupted migration, malformed payloads, checksums, counts, duplicates, and family-specific typed errors are independently testable.
V2 reads an approved V1 representation and writes its new format only after manifest/checksum validation; it never opens V1 files directly.
public_contract.compatibility: Logical migration compatibility is required and unresolved until Recovery Receipts and parity tests exist.

risk.description: Family transfer is where silent omission becomes permanent data loss and generic errors make repair unsafe.
